target_customer: Building material distributors, suppliers and contractors that need same-day local delivery of heavy or bulky goods
problem: Construction trades lose time driving to pick up supplies, and distributors lack flexible local delivery capacity. Curri matches loads to a network of independent drivers and trucks on demand.
business_model: On-demand logistics marketplace with delivery fees, later dedicated fleets, carrier management software and an API

founders.name: Matt Lafferty
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CEO by FreightWaves and TechCrunch. Background not found in opened sources.

founders.name: Brian Gonzalez
founders.background_notes: YC page lists engineering leadership at Dollar Shave Club and Geni, focused on product, engineering and design.

competitors.name: RenoRun
competitors.what: Montreal based delivery service for construction and renovation materials
competitors.funding_then: Reported 22.5M CAD Series A by November 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Dispatch and matching marketplace with driver supply, routing and tracking; standard engineering with hard operational parts at scale.

defensibility.rationale: Delivery marketplaces are copyable; advantage came from driver supply density and distributor integrations built over time.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Sources found do not show a large player taking the construction delivery wedge as of 2023; Curri raised a Series B in 2023.

market_need_then: Founders reported that tradespeople spent hours driving for supplies and a plumber interview in late 2018 shaped the focus. FreightWaves described a fragmented market with costly in-house fleets as the alternative.

identity.logo: Wordmark with a green accent color per site assets
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and trust focused: Move the world's goods with speed, intelligence, and trust

brand_strength.rationale: Mostly B2B with no press about the brand itself found; the About page says only that the founders named it Curri without explanation.

outcome_analysis: Curri found a clear niche in construction supply delivery after talking with tradespeople in late 2018, joined YC in Summer 2019, raised a 6M Series A in 2021 and a 42M Series B led by Bessemer in 2023. It reports revenue growth and about 110 staff and remains active, with no layoffs or exit found in searches.
notes: Aggregators (Clay, Clera, VCBacked) date the Series B to July 2024; TechCrunch and CB Insights say June 2023, used here. Total raised per TechCrunch is 48.2M, about 6.2M above the Series A; the earlier seed is not found. YC page lists Curri founded 2018. Competitor source date is the date of the event it reports; the Onfleet post itself is undated. Outcome search found no layoffs or exit.
